2026-08-11T03:43:02.0442499Z ## MCP Servers Mounted as Shell CLI Commands
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0443215Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0443996Z The following servers are available as CLI commands on `PATH`:
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0444915Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0445605Z - `safeoutputs` — run `safeoutputs --help` to see available tools
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0446554Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0449410Z > **IMPORTANT**: For `safeoutputs` and `mcpscripts`, **always use the CLI commands** listed above instead of the equivalent MCP tools. The CLI wrappers are the preferred interface — do **not** call their MCP tools directly even though they may appear in your tool list.
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0452749Z >
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0457392Z > For `safeoutputs`, treat every successful command as a real write-intent declaration. Do **not** use `safeoutputs` for exploratory probing, auth checks, placeholder payloads, repeated "try again" variants, or manual runtime experiments. When you need a safe-output, emit the final intended call once. If you are not ready to perform the real action, use `noop` or `report_incomplete` instead.
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0462115Z >
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0463774Z > For all other servers listed here, they are **only** available as CLI commands and are **not** available as MCP tools.
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0465233Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0465584Z ### How to Use
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0466032Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0467235Z Each server is a standalone executable on your `PATH`. Invoke it from bash like any other shell command:
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0468594Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0468930Z ```bash
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0470171Z # Call a tool — pass arguments as --name value pairs
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0471547Z <server-name> <tool-name> --param1 value1 --param2 value2
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0472724Z ```
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0473123Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0473779Z **Example** — using the `playwright` CLI:
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0474824Z ```bash
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0475875Z playwright --help                                  # list all browser tools
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0477401Z playwright browser_navigate --url https://example.com
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0479016Z playwright browser_snapshot                        # capture page accessibility tree
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0481466Z ```
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0481957Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0483219Z **Example** — using the `safeoutputs` CLI (safe outputs) when you are ready to emit the final real action:
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0485169Z ```bash
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0486246Z safeoutputs add_comment --issue_number 42 --body "Analysis complete"
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0487569Z ```
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0487971Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0488746Z **Example** — using the `mcpscripts` CLI (mcp-scripts):
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0489904Z ```bash
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0490933Z mcpscripts --help                                  # list all script tools
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0492634Z mcpscripts mcpscripts-gh --args "pr list --repo owner/repo --limit 5"
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0494212Z ```
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0494613Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0495135Z ### Passing Multiple or Complex Arguments (Preferred)
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0495951Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0498753Z **Preferred approach for any tool call with multiple or complex arguments**: supply a JSON object on stdin using `.` as the sentinel. The bridge parses stdin as the argument object, preserving all native types (numbers, booleans, arrays) without shell-quoting issues.
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0501833Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0502169Z ```bash
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0503049Z # Full argument payload as JSON via printf pipe
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0504868Z printf '{"issue_number":42,"body":"### Title\n\nBody paragraph one.\n\nBody paragraph two."}' \
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0506460Z   | safeoutputs add_comment .
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0507062Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0507905Z # Works with any tool — just match the parameter names from <server> <tool> --help
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0509852Z printf '{"title":"Fix: something","body":"Details here","labels":["bug","priority-high"]}' \
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0511423Z   | safeoutputs create_issue .
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0512339Z ```
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0512734Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0514343Z **When pipes are blocked by the bash security policy**, write the payload to a file first and use **file redirection** with the `.` sentinel instead:
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0516119Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0516458Z ```bash
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0517707Z # Step 1 — write the JSON payload to a file using the Write tool or a bash heredoc
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0519368Z # Step 2 — redirect the file into the CLI command using '<'
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0520739Z safeoutputs create_pull_request . < /tmp/payload.json
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0521579Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0522334Z # This is equivalent to piping but does not require a separate command before '|'
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0524037Z safeoutputs add_comment . < /tmp/comment.json
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0525111Z ```
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0525514Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0525917Z > **Why prefer JSON payload mode?**
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0527401Z > - Single operation for any number of arguments — no repeated `--key value` flags
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0529252Z > - Native types (integers, booleans, arrays) are preserved exactly as specified
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0531207Z > - No shell quoting or escaping needed for newlines, quotes, or special characters
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0533133Z > - Agents can construct the payload as a structured object before emitting the command
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0535262Z > - File redirection (`< file`) works even when pipes (`|`) are restricted
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0536307Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0536647Z ### Notes
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0537066Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0538267Z - **Prefer JSON payload mode** (`. < file` or `printf '{...}' | server tool .`) for any call with multiple arguments or complex values
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0540981Z - All parameters can also be passed as `--name value` pairs; boolean flags can be set with `--flag` (no value) to mean `true`
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0543386Z - Use `.` as the only argument to parse stdin as a JSON object (all parameters supplied at once)
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0545986Z - Parameter names with hyphens or underscores are interchangeable (e.g. `issue-number` and `issue_number` both work)
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0548290Z - Output is printed to stdout; errors are printed to stderr with a non-zero exit code
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0550349Z - Run the CLI commands inside a `bash` tool call — they are shell executables, not MCP tools
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0552219Z - These CLI commands are read-only and cannot be modified by the agent
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0553961Z </mcp-clis>
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0555491Z <github-context>
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0556714Z The following GitHub context information is available for this workflow:

2026-08-11T03:43:02.0582642Z ## Instructions
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0583088Z 
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0583982Z Create a daily digest workflow for professional developers, referencing
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0585700Z relevant top Hacker News stories on technology that can be used today
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0587333Z by large companies. Every weekday, fetch the top 30 stories from the
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0589166Z Hacker News API (https://hacker-news.firebaseio.com/v0/topstories.json),
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0590849Z filter to stories with a score above 100 that are about software
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0592419Z engineering, cloud infrastructure, AI/ML, developer tooling, or
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0594214Z distributed systems. For each qualifying story include: the title, the
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0595889Z URL, the score, the number of comments, and a one-sentence summary of
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0597460Z why it is relevant to enterprise developers. Create a GitHub issue
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0599108Z titled "HN Digest – <date>" with the results formatted as a Markdown
2026-08-11T03:43:02.0600377Z table.
